rationale: Evidence: four races (iterations 0 to 3, 240 trials) all ended off track. Progress stays at 0.10 to 0.16 and max_error at 0.061 to 0.067 m whatever the base_speed (1.6, 1.4, 1.2, 1.0), kp (4.0, 3.5, 2.5), ki (0.05 to 0.2) or sensor footprint (0.012 or 0.016). So speed and gain are not the binding limit. The most recent race (iteration 3, score 52.06) shows steering_oscillation of 0.139 on the s-bend and 0.143 on the slalom, against 0.075 on the oval. The Evaluator's rule for this case is to raise kd toward 0.4 before changing kp or base_speed, and iteration 1 showed kd 0.3 reduced oval oscillation. Change: kd 0.3 to 0.4. Everything else stays as in iteration 3 (geometry unchanged, kp 2.5, ki 0.2, base_speed 1.0, sensor_size 0.012, line_loss last_direction), so this is a single-lever test of damping on the bends. Expected result: steering_oscillation on the s-bend and slalom falls below about 0.12, and progress rises modestly, perhaps to 0.2 or more on the s-bend. Completion in 3 s is not expected at base_speed 1.0. Hypotheses: (a) the bend drift is driven by a fast jitter/overshoot loop that derivative damping can remove; (b) if progress still sits near 0.15 with low oscillation, the limit is geometric (sensors only 0.05 m ahead of the axle, so the robot reacts late on curves), and the next test should move the sensor row forward (y 0.07) or change wheel_track. Measurements wanted per track and per seed: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort, so I can see where on each track the run ends.
